event_confirmation: Company release 2026-10-16 (Business Wire via Finviz): Q3 2026 results after the close Thursday 2026-10-22, call Friday 2026-10-23 10:00 CT. https://finviz.com/news/403693/comfort-systems-usa-announces-third-quarter-2026-conference-call-and-webcast
conviction_note: Each side of the evidence offsets the other. A likely revenue beat on a fast-growing backlog (Q2 backlog +13% q/q, consensus implying only +2.6-4.1% sequential revenue) and a 22% pre-print derating sit against three things: elevated estimate-change catch-ups (7.7-8.1% of revenue in H1 2026 against 4.0% in Q3 2025) that put the margin's quality at risk, a reaction function that sold the last two beats (-2.7%, -5.3% on an 11% revenue beat), and an AI-infrastructure tape that is selling beats on the print day itself (Nokia -10% on a beat, XLK -3% on 10-22). The findings sum to -0.2 and p_up is 50, so the scaled number is 0. The two measurements agree; abs_move stays at the option-implied 11.5% because uncertainty about the sign does not shrink the size of the move.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $3.35-3.40bn and EPS $12.70-12.85. Zacks: $3.35bn / $12.70 (Yahoo/Zacks, 2026-10-19, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/comfort-systems-stock-q3-earnings-123800494.html). GuruFocus: $3.4bn / $12.85 (2026-10-21, https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9135280/comfort-systems-fix-set-to-report-q3-earnings-amid-strong-growth-and-high-valuation). Barchart had EPS $12.42 on 2026-10-05, older. The two current sources agree to within 1.5%. The company guide is FY2026 same-store revenue growth 'mid-to-high 30%' (Q2 call, TIKR 2026-07-25, https://www.tikr.com/blog/comfort-systems-q2-earnings-crossed-3-billion-for-the-first-time-the-backlog-says-more-is-coming); with H1 same-store at +47%, that implies H2 in the high-20s to low-30s. FY consensus at +42.1% already sits above the guide, so the street expects another raise. No company numeric quarterly guide exists.
positioning_check: Short interest 849,979 shares, 2.4% of shares outstanding, days to cover 2.61 at the 2026-09-30 settlement (2.82 on 09-15), per Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/fix/shortinterest, read 2026-10-22). This is not a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d is +0.55 vol points and put/call OI 1.23: balanced, with no directional statement from the options. Event-implied move 11.5% (straddle 16.53% to the 11-20 expiry). Tape: -13.56% over 5 days, -22.09% over 20 days, -38% from the 52-week high. Market cap was $69.8bn on 10-05 (Barchart) and is about $45bn at the sealed spot of $1,280. Zacks Rank 4 (Sell), ESP 0.00%.

findings.finding: The consensus revenue bar ($3.35-3.40bn) implies only +2.6-4.1% sequential growth over Q2's $3.27bn. Q2 ended with record backlog of $14.06bn, +$1.61bn (+13%) q/q, and Q1 to Q2 revenue grew +14%. FIX has beaten revenue every quarter, including Q2 by 11% ($3.27bn against $2.94bn), so the arithmetic points to another revenue beat of a few percent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold in 2026: Q1 (2026-04-23) -2.69% and Q2 (2026-07-23) -5.33% on an 11% revenue beat with backlog +13% q/q. In 2025 the same line bought +22.4% (Jul) and +19.0% (Oct). The response has turned from strongly positive to negative as the multiple stretched.
findings.why_not_priced: The beat itself is largely expected (nine upward estimate revisions in three months; the street's FY sits above the guide). What is not in consensus is the size of the sequential step: if the market had priced Q2's backlog burn, Q3 estimates would sit nearer $3.5bn than $3.35-3.40bn. This is sized small because the name has sold its last two beats.
findings.independence: Census data-center construction spending accelerating to +73% y/y in August (https://www.neoteo.com/en/us-data-center-construction-hit-a-reported-record-annual-pace-in-august) points the same way from a different source. The consensus figures come from Zacks/Yahoo 2026-10-19.

findings.finding: Revenue from estimate changes on prior-period performance obligations (catch-ups) added 8.1% of revenue in Q1 2026 and 7.7% in Q2 2026, against 4.0% in Q3 2025, 4.4% in Q2 2025 and 1.7% in Q3 2024. About $230-250m a quarter of H1 revenue, at high incremental margin, came from favourable re-estimates. That puts the quality of the 25.9-26.3% gross margin at risk if Q3 catch-ups revert toward the 4% of a year ago, which would take roughly 2-4 points of revenue and some margin off the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior case of margin disappointing on FIX in the baseline. The last two prints, with gross margin at records (Q1 26.3%, Q2 25.9%), still fell -2.7% and -5.3%, so the market was already discounting margin quality.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure sits in the revenue-recognition note of the 10-Qs and appears in no release, preview or call highlight read here. Previews quote the gross margin and the backlog, not the share of revenue from re-estimates. If it were priced, Q3 consensus EPS ($12.70-12.85, slightly above Q2's $12.53 on +3-4% revenue) would imply margin compression rather than a flat-to-up margin.
findings.independence: The Q1 10-Q (8.1% vs 5.8%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035983/000110465926047689/fix-20260331x10q.htm) and the Q3 2025 10-Q (4.0% vs 1.7%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035983/000110465925101821/fix-20250930x10q.htm) are the same company's documents, not independent confirmation. The counter-reading is that sustained catch-ups reflect strong project execution, which would mean no reversion. Nothing external confirms a reversion.

findings.finding: The FY2026 same-store growth guide (mid-to-high 30%, set on the Q2 call) is below where consensus sits (+42.1% FY revenue). H1 same-store was +47%, so a raise or firming of the FY guide with a first 2027 read is the likely forward-looking content of this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 guide raise (to mid-to-high 30% from mid-to-high teens in February) came with -5.33%. The Feb 2026 initial guide of mid-to-high teens came with +6.46%.
findings.why_not_priced: A raise is partly expected because consensus already sits above the guide. The unpriced part is the 2027 tone after a quarter in which data-center planning cooled (Dodge) and the stock lost about 30% of its value. A firm 2027 read would be visible as a narrowing of the 11.5% implied move toward the upside, which the balanced skew does not show.
findings.independence: The FY consensus growth comes from Zacks/Yahoo 2026-10-19 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/comfort-systems-stock-q3-earnings-123800494.html). The guide comes from the Q2 call.

findings.finding: Into the print, the stock fell from about $69.8bn market cap (10-05) to about $45bn at the sealed spot: -22% over 20 days, -13.6% over 5 days, and about -8.6% intraday on 10-22 alone ($1,401 on 10-21 to $1,280). There was no company-specific news; the only stock-specific item was Goldman's target cut to $1,875 from $2,159 on 10-20 for 'multiple compression' while keeping Buy. A derating of this size lowers the multiple bar that sold the last two beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the baseline, the large positive reactions (+22.4% Jul 2025, +19.0% Oct 2025) came when the stock had not run ahead of fundamentals. The 2026 negative reactions came near highs ($1,756 in July). Today's setup, 38% off the high, has no direct precedent in the eight prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price, so this finding is about the bar rather than new information. It is filed small because the drawdown has a sector cause (rates, AI-capex financing) that a single quarter does not fix. If the derating were fully reflected in expectations, the sell-side would have cut estimates; instead, estimates were revised up nine times in three months while only the targets came down.
findings.independence: Market cap of $69.8bn on 10-05 per Barchart/Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/earnings-preview-expect-comfort-systems-121230776.html) and $49.32bn on 10-21 per GuruFocus. The 'bar is lower' reading is an inference, not a document.

findings.finding: The print lands into a tape that is selling AI-infrastructure beats. On 10-22 the S&P 500 was -1.37% and XLK about -3% on broad AI selling, and Nokia fell about 10% the same morning despite a data-center-driven beat ($5.79bn revenue against $5.07bn consensus, AI & Cloud +123%), on cash conversion. Vertiv had an 11-session record losing streak into 10-20. AI power names (GEV -11%, VRT -14%, BE -15%) fell in the week to 10-20 on rate and AI-financing fears.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FIX fell -5.33% on a large Q2 beat when the AI tape was still strong. Peers on 10-22 show the same 'beat and sell' response.
findings.why_not_priced: The tape is in the price up to the seal. What is not priced is the next session's macro and sector drift, which the trade holds through the 10-23 close. If the market had already discounted that, the skew would lean to puts; it is balanced at +0.55.
findings.independence: Yahoo, 2026-10-22: GE Vernova -11%, Vertiv -14%, Bloom -15% in the week, with AI-financing and rate fears (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ge-vernova-sinks-11-vertiv-134456087.html). The NextDC -40% on Melbourne site delays (newspaceeconomy.ca, 2026-10-22) is folded in here as tape.

findings.finding: Dodge Momentum Index for September 2026 (released 10-07): commercial planning -1.3% m/m and -3.0% y/y, with data centers named as the drag ('slower planning momentum after a surge in late 2025'). August's index was down 0.4% on 'weaker data center planning' and was revised lower. Ex-data-centers, commercial planning was -14.9% y/y, so data centers are still growing y/y but decelerating. This is the bookings/backlog line for FIX's Q3 (58.7% of Q2 revenue was Technology).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog is the line FIX trades on. Backlog +13% q/q in Q2 still came with -5.33%; there is no record of a backlog decline in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Planning indices are not in the earnings previews, which anchor on 'record backlog'. If priced, Q3 backlog expectations would be published as flat-to-down sequentially; no preview read gives a backlog estimate at all. This is filed small because it is a planning proxy rather than FIX's own bookings, and FIX's modular work books further out.
findings.independence: Dodge, August release, 2026-09-08 (https://inside.lighting/news/26-09/construction-planning-shifts-beyond-data-center-boom). Same index provider, so not independent. GE Vernova's CEO saying data centers' share of Electrification orders falls to about 20% in Q3 is filed separately.

findings.finding: GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said data centers' share of Electrification orders would fall to 'probably more like 20%' in Q3 2026. This is a read from an adjacent supplier into the same customers, on a quarter that covers FIX's Q3 bookings period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. FIX's backlog has been the stock's driver.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is in a GE Vernova context, not FIX's. It is sized small because a lower share of GEV orders could mean lumpiness rather than a lower absolute level, and GEV is a different part of the build (grid equipment, not MEP).
findings.independence: Dodge planning slowdown (inside.lighting, 2026-10-07) points the same way. Census spending +73% y/y points the other way.

findings.finding: Census construction spending: private data-center construction reached a record $84.95bn SAAR in August 2026, +73% y/y, accelerating from +36% (May), +55% (Jun) and +65% (Jul). That is the work-in-place series that maps to FIX's revenue burn in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been sold in 2026 (-2.7%, -5.3%), so a confirmed strong burn has been worth little on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a broad public series (released 10-01), so it is mostly priced. It sits beside the Dodge planning series as the broader current-activity series, as the lessons require. If it were not priced, consensus Q3 revenue growth would sit below +36.7% y/y; it does not.
findings.independence: AGC analysis of the same Census release: +7.5% m/m, +73% y/y (search snippet). Same underlying data.

findings.finding: Johnson Controls (reported 2026-07-29, after FIX's last call): orders +27%, Americas orders +37% 'supported by data-center and other mission-critical demand', record backlog $21bn. A counterparty in commercial HVAC equipment for the same buildings FIX installs into.
findings.why_not_priced: It is three months old and public, so mostly priced. Filed because it postdates FIX's last word and covers part of FIX's Q3 bookings window.
findings.independence: SpaceX and Super Micro (10-21) are a separate source with the same direction.

findings.finding: AI-capex demand prints on 10-21: SpaceX guided Q4 capex of $35-40bn, mostly AI compute, and Super Micro raised fiscal Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5bn, about $4bn above its prior range. Vertiv rose 7% on it, but FIX fell from about $1,401 to $1,280 through the next session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. FIX did not participate in the 10-21 bounce.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and one day old, and the market sold FIX through it, so it is a weak macro-to-company transmission (servers and capex, not MEP construction). Small.
findings.independence: Census +73% y/y is a separate series with the same direction. Single source for the Super Micro figure (an IBTimes report; not confirmed on Super Micro's own release here).

findings.finding: Billings in excess of costs plus deferred revenue jumped $1.11bn in H1 2026, to $3.23bn from $2.12bn, which drove the $1.14bn Q2 operating cash flow. CFO Bill George attributed it to advance customer cash and said cash flow should align with net income plus non-cash items over time. A Q3 OCF that reverses toward earnings is the likely outcome, and a cash-conversion headline is what sank Nokia on 10-22.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record cash flow came with -5.33%, so the market did not pay for the cash. It may not punish a reversal either.
findings.why_not_priced: Management pre-warned that the cash is timing, so a reversal sits inside what the company has said. Hence the near-zero size.
findings.independence: This shares the Q2 10-Q with the catch-up finding, but it is a different line (balance sheet and cash flow, not revenue recognition). Nasdaq call summary (search snippet) for the CFO remark.

findings.finding: Insider selling after the last print: Form 144s on 08-10, 08-11, 08-17 and 08-26, with Form 4s on 08-12, 08-18 and 08-27. GuruFocus puts insider sales at $178.4m over 12 months, with no purchases.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine post-print window selling, public for two months, at prices well above today's. Close to zero.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the balanced skew (+0.55) and splits on the run-up. The 22% derating lowers the multiple bar, while the same AI-capex fears behind it are still selling beats on the print day, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): revenue-beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5 because FIX sold its last two beats (-2.7%, -5.3% on an 11% beat); p_up from 52 to 50.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy below broad series): Dodge planning finding cut from -1.0 to -0.4 after reading the release (data centers still growing y/y; Census work-in-place +73% y/y is the broader current series). GE Vernova proxy cut from -0.4 to -0.3; JCI and SpaceX/Super Micro proxies cut from +0.5 to +0.3 each.
Rule 5 (absence of explanation is not evidence): the 'washout lowers the bar' positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.4, because the drawdown has a sector cause.
Rule 1 / tape: AI-tape 'beats sold' finding moved from -1.0 to -0.8 so it is not counted twice against the reaction-history caveat already applied to the revenue finding.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): OCF reversal cut from -0.3 to -0.2, because the CFO pre-announced that cash would align over time; insider sales cut from -0.2 to -0.1 as stale.

Left standing: the 10-Q catch-up finding (-1.0), a primary-document number of the kind the file says has paid, and the guidance finding (+0.5). print_vs_bar cut from +4 to +3 to net the catch-up reversion risk.
Rule 7: short interest checked (2.4%, DTC 2.6); not crowded, so no shrink of the negatives on squeeze grounds.
